content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

What I found:
- **§ 2(d) (p0029)** is the only ownership provision and runs one way — TrueLink retains ownership of the Interface. That part is fine (Vendor background IP).
- There is **no reciprocal statement** that Client owns Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property, or the borrower/credit data flowing through the Interface, and **no ownership of or licence to the results of the Support Services** Client pays for.
- The nearest support is confidentiality only (§ 10(b)/(c) deem "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" Client Proprietary Information) plus a termination-only line in § 13 ("Client shall retain full ownership of all domains associated with Client and Client Content"). Confidential treatment and a termination carve-out are not ownership, so the Agreement fails even the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free right to use, modify and sublicense work product).

Redline (validated ok:true): a new § 2(e) "Client Ownership" inserted after § 2(d) confirming our retained rights in content, IP and data (expressly subject to the existing § 8(d) licence so no conflict arises), assigning Support Services work product to Client with a licence back for embedded TrueLink IP, and negating any transfer to TrueLink or joint ownership.

Noted but not separately flagged: the § 8(d) grant letting TrueLink "resell, exploit" Credit Data is a licence (bounded by the Non-Competition Agreement), not an assignment — a data-use point for the data rule rather than an ownership breach.
